title: red-first names the task's own case by its label, and reads only the runner that ran
desiredOutcome: stamp-verification red recognises a house case whose label starts with an ordinary word as the task's own, and an expected ERROR: line from a passing house case is no longer counted as a failing unittest case, so a genuine red-first reads proved.

tasks.title: red-first reads a house case by its full label and the unittest reader only on unittest output
tasks.description: stamp-verification.failing_cases takes label.split()[0] as a house case's id, so a label that is a sentence starting with an ordinary word ('the', 'a') gets an id that also exists in HEAD's test file and the task's own case is never recognised; and _UNITTEST_CASE (^(FAIL|ERROR): ) is applied to every output, so a house suite whose PASSING case prints 'ERROR: <path> is not a directory' as expected stdout gets a phantom failing case. Reported on P78.9 (a new house case 'the gate-economy row is wired into diagnose() ...' read could-not-prove, exit 3, while the raw run had exactly that one FAIL line). Fix: a house case is identified by its FULL label, with a leading id-shaped token (letters then digits, e.g. me1, ga9b) used as its id only when present; the task's own case is matched by either; the unittest FAIL:/ERROR: reader applies only when the output is unittest-shaped (a 'Ran N tests' line). Cases both ways: a sentence label proves red, an id-led label is still named by its id, a house run with an expected ERROR: line counts no phantom, a real unittest ERROR: is still counted and not credited as an assertion.
